comparison: Both address bulk RNASeq data showing CMF gene expression in cardiac ECs (C26-C39). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with multiple independent datasets and correlation analyses arguing against contamination. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, expressing significant concerns about potential cardiomyocyte contamination and requesting more rigorous experimentation to rule out doublets and cell-free RNA artifacts.

Both evaluate single-cell analysis of CMF gene expression (C40-C50). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, emphasizing unspliced transcripts as compelling evidence for cell-intrinsic transcription. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, maintaining concerns about contamination from cardiomyocyte-EC doublets or RNA capture by EC glycocalyx, and requesting additional experiments like RNAse treatment.

Both assess nuclear isolation and in situ hybridization data (C51-C60). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, viewing these orthogonal approaches as definitively ruling out contamination. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, acknowledging improvements after revision but maintaining concerns about specificity and requesting Z-plane views and higher resolution imaging with junction markers.

Both evaluate ATAC-Seq chromatin accessibility data (C61-C72). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, emphasizing open chromatin at CMF genes and motif enrichment as strong evidence for active transcription. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, concerned about bulk ATAC-seq contamination and requesting dual single-cell RNA and ATAC-seq, plus questioning why closed chromatin appears at some active genes.

Both address the comparison of gene expression with chromatin accessibility (C73-C75). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as internal validation distinguishing true EC expression from artifacts. Peer reviewers also rate this SUPPORTED, accepting this analysis without specific challenges as evidence correlating chromatin accessibility with genuine expression.

Both evaluate culture experiments showing loss of CMF chromatin accessibility (C77-C84). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, viewing selective closure of CMF genes as evidence for in vivo environmental cues. Peer reviewers also rate this SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretation without raising specific concerns about the culture data.

Both address the stochastic transcription model (C89-C92). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED but notes it relies on comparing bulk and single-cell data with different sensitivities. Peer reviewers also rate this SUPPORTED, accepting the model as a reasonable explanation reconciling bulk ATAC-seq and single-cell RNA-seq observations.

Both evaluate developmental and mechanistic hypotheses (C93-C95, C105-C106). OpenEval rates this UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly stated hypotheses that remain speculative. Peer reviewers rate this SUPPORTED, not challenging the hypotheses which are appropriately presented as speculative interpretations requiring experimental validation.

Both address the overarching conclusion about cell-autonomous CMF gene expression (C7, C8, C85-C86). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED by convergence of multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, requesting authors temper conclusions to better reflect that the work focuses on transcriptional/epigenetic regulation while protein translation and function remain open questions.

OpenEval R12 addresses authors' acknowledgment of limitations regarding protein translation and function (C24, C88), rating this SUPPORTED as appropriate caveats. Peer R7 overlaps on C88, with reviewers requesting the Discussion be amended to emphasize that protein translation/function remains an open question.

OpenEval R10 evaluates citation of published literature on MEF2C and GATA4 roles (C96-C104), rating this SUPPORTED as appropriate integration of prior work. Peer R9 partially overlaps (C96-C97) and does not challenge these citations, accepting them as supporting the mechanistic hypothesis.

OpenEval R11 addresses background knowledge and field context (C1-C2, C9-C23, C87), rating this SUPPORTED as accurate description of prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.
